excerpt: Virgin R-134a in a 30-pound cylinder with a 1/4 ACME fitting, factory sealed, made in the USA and certified as compliant with EPA regulations.
description:
A 30-pound cylinder of R-134a with a 1/4 ACME fitting, factory sealed and filled with virgin refrigerant. It is made in the USA and certified as compliant with EPA regulations.
Thirty pounds is a working stock size rather than a single-repair size, which puts this cylinder in shops handling HVAC service, automotive air conditioning and commercial refrigeration through a season. Home24Care lists it as a professional-grade refrigerant for professional and commercial use.
what_changed: Removed the fabricated compatibility guidance "The 1/4 ACME connection is stated in the title so you can confirm it matches the hoses and manifold you already run before the cylinder ships" - the source says nothing about hoses, manifolds or checking fitment (and the clause also carried a shipping reference). Replaced with a source-backed line: the product is listed as professional-grade for professional and commercial use. Excerpt untouched.

excerpt: A 10x10 galvanized steel louvered pergola with drainage and gutter guards in the posts, rated to 2,000 pounds and 100 mph winds under a 5-year warranty.
description:
The louvers on the Sarasota are adjustable: open them to let filtered sunlight through, or close them completely for shade and weather protection. The structure itself is heavy-duty galvanized steel rather than wood.
That steel is powder-coated through the posts and anchoring plates as well as the roof, giving a black finish that is rust and corrosion resistant and needs no maintenance. Rainwater runs into downspouts inside the steel posts, and gutter guards keep debris from blocking them. Pro-Tect testing rates this 10x10 at 2,000 pounds of roof weight and 100 mph wind speeds.
The patented PowerPort supplies three electrical outlets and USB ports for lights or speakers. It ships ready to assemble with BILT app instructions and carries a 5-year warranty.
what_changed: Rewrote the opening so the louvre description states only what the source states - adjustable louvers that open for filtered sunlight or close completely for shade and weather protection - dropping the broader "Shade on the Sarasota is adjustable" framing, which implied a range of positions the source never describes. Also removed "freestanding" from the excerpt: the source only mentions posts and anchoring plates, and the wall-mounted Evanston has posts too, so nothing establishes it; replaced with "galvanized", which the source does state. Paragraphs two and three unchanged.

excerpt: The 12x10 Stratford is a black powder-coated galvanized steel pergola with traditional proportions and steel up to 30% thicker than mass-produced kits.
description:
The 12x10 Stratford is sized for a patio or a dining area rather than a whole yard. The proportions follow traditional architecture, and the posts, beams, and rafters are sized so the structure carries visual weight instead of reading as a light frame.
Construction is fully powder-coated galvanized steel in black, with material up to 30% thicker than typical mass-produced options and part profiles three times larger than standard small-footprint kits. Components are tested for long-term durability, including performance in high winds and coastal environments.
what_changed: Deleted the invented finish sentence "The black finish draws a defined outline against pale siding, stone, and planting" - the source describes no finish behaviour and the title supplies only the colour, which is now carried by "powder-coated galvanized steel in black". Also dropped "the smallest of the four Stratford sizes": the size-lineup count comes from the catalog assortment, not from the source copy or title. Excerpt unchanged.

excerpt: This 16x12 black pergola uses steel part profiles three times larger than standard small-footprint kits, on a fully powder-coated galvanized frame.
description:
Part size is what separates the Stratford from a flat-pack pergola, and it shows most at 16x12. The profiles are three times larger than those used in standard small-footprint kits, and the steel itself runs up to 30% thicker than typical mass-produced options, so a span this wide keeps the proportions of traditional architecture instead of thinning out.
The frame is galvanized steel under a full powder coat in black. Components are tested for long-term durability and reliable performance in harsh conditions, including high winds and coastal environments. Sixteen by twelve leaves depth for a full seating layout and length to spare along the back of a house.
what_changed: Rewrote the excerpt to drop "The largest of the four Stratford sizes" - a superlative and a size count that exist nowhere in the source (byte-identical across all eight Stratford SKUs) or the title, and that would silently go wrong if the lineup changes; it now leads on the part-profile fact the source does state. The description was left alone: its construction and finish claims (fully powder-coated galvanized steel, 30% thicker material, 3x part profiles, high-wind and coastal testing, black from the title) all trace to the source.

excerpt: A cedar playhouse with a working half door, snack bar window, toy kitchen accessories, and flowerpot holders, shipping pre-cut, pre-stained and pre-drilled.
description:
The Sweetwater Playhouse is cedar, finished light brown with black trim. A working half door makes the entrance, large windows let in light and moving air, and the snack bar window turns the place into a cafe or a tea party depending on the game being played that afternoon.
Inside are a toy sink, a stove, a cordless phone, and an assortment of other accessories to work with. Flowerpot holders on the exterior give young gardeners somewhere to put their pots. The pieces arrive pre-cut, pre-stained, and pre-drilled, so putting it together is mostly a matter of working through the sequence in order.
what_changed: Cut the invented "cafe counter" - the source names a snack bar window and mentions tea parties and running a cafe, but no counter component - so the window now simply turns the place into a cafe or a tea party. Also removed the fabricated size language: "keeps to a small footprint" in the description and "compact" in the excerpt, neither of which has any anchor in a source that contains no dimension, footprint or size wording at all. Everything else (cedar, light brown finish, black trim, half door, windows, toy sink/stove/phone, flowerpot holders, pre-cut/pre-stained/pre-drilled) is source-backed and untouched.

excerpt: An all-cedar 20x12 pergola with a trellis roof, powder-coated steel anchoring plates, a 100 mph wind rating, and a PowerPort with three outlets and three USB ports.
description: Dual structural cross beams, heavy support posts, and corbels carry the trellis roof on the 20x12 Beaumont, a pergola built from 100% cedar. The open roof slats filter sunlight into a mix of light and shade over a patio or seating area, and they give climbing vines and hanging pots something to grab. Cedar brings its own resistance to decay, and thick powder-coated steel anchoring plates hold the posts down; Pro-Tect testing rates the structure to winds of up to 100 mph. The patented PowerPort adds three USB ports and three electrical outlets for lighting, speakers, and other accessories. Every piece arrives pre-cut, pre-drilled, and pre-stained, with guided instructions in the interactive BILT app.
what_changed: Changed "carved corbels" to "corbels". The source says only "dual structural cross beams, robust support posts, and elegant corbels" - nothing states the corbels are carved, which asserts a finishing detail about a physical component the manufacturer copy does not claim. One-word fix; the rest of the paragraph (cedar, wind rating, anchoring plates, PowerPort counts, pre-cut components, BILT app) is unchanged and source-backed.

excerpt: A two-level Nordic spruce playset with a canopy-roofed clubhouse, a lower room with a front door, an 8-foot wave slide and two rope-hung belt swings.

Two levels of play. Up top is an elevated clubhouse under a canopy roof; underneath it is a lower play space with a full front door of its own, which is the part that makes it read as a small house rather than a platform on legs.
A spacious side window is set up as a snack bar. The slide is an 8-foot wave slide, and two classic belt swings hang on rope chains chosen to be gentle on small hands.
The wood is robust Nordic spruce, finished in a light brown stain.
what_changed: Fixed the play-feature line: "A spacious side window on the lower level is set up as a snack bar counter" became "A spacious side window is set up as a snack bar" - the source says only "A spacious side window designed with a snack bar", never placing it on the lower level and never mentioning a counter. Also ended the wood sentence at the fact: "The wood is robust Nordic spruce, finished in a light brown stain." The old claim that Backyard Discovery uses cedar on its larger sets is absent from the source and false against the catalog, where larger, pricier sets (Dover Bay, Spruce Hollow) are also spruce.

excerpt: Emory's corner island in the right-hand orientation, pairing a built-in grill with bar seating on a galvanized steel frame rated for year-round weather.

Fully powder-coated galvanized steel, engineered to handle extreme weather year-round, is the starting point for this Emory island. Range tests every component in the build, appliances and frame included.
On top of that structure sits a built-in grill, a run of counter space, storage cabinets with soft-close hardware, and outdoor-rated refrigeration. The island also carries bar seating.
This is the right-hand orientation. The left-hand version is a separate listing.

excerpt: A cedar playhouse in white with black trim, with a working half door, snack bar window, flowerpot holders, and a toy sink, stove, and phone inside.
description:
Cedar construction finished in white with black trim gives the Sweetwater Playhouse the look of a small cottage rather than a plastic play structure. Backyard Discovery fits it with large windows that keep the interior bright and let a breeze move through on warm days. Decorative flowerpot holders sit on the outside for children who want to plant something, and a working half door gives them an entrance of their own. A snack bar window is where most of the pretend cafe and tea party business ends up happening.
Inside there is a toy sink, a stove, a cordless phone, and a range of other play accessories. Pieces arrive pre-cut, pre-stained, and pre-drilled, so putting it together is a matter of following the sequence rather than cutting and finishing lumber yourself.
what_changed: Trimmed "A snack bar window along one wall opens onto a counter, which is where..." to "A snack bar window is where...". The source names only "The snack bar window" and its tea party and cafe play - it never mentions a counter (a separate physical component) and never says which wall the window is on. Nothing else in the entry was altered.

excerpt: A 10-foot yellow wave slide from Backyard Discovery, of one-piece construction with high side walls and designed to hold a rider up to 250 pounds.
description: A 10-foot wave slide in yellow, made by Backyard Discovery for use on a swing set. The wave shape gives a rolling ride down rather than a straight drop, and the high side walls keep the rider in place through it. One-piece construction means there are no sections to join during installation. It is designed to hold 250 pounds.

excerpt: A 16x12 Beaumont in 100 percent cedar, with a trellis roof for climbing vines and powder-coated steel anchoring plates rated to withstand 100 mph winds.
description:
Cedar throughout and open overhead, the Beaumont covers a patio without closing it in. Its trellis roof filters sunlight into a mix of light and shade, and the crosspieces take climbing vines or hanging planters for anyone who wants the structure to green over.
Strength comes from dual structural cross beams, robust support posts and corbels, all in 100 percent cedar that resists decay. Thick powder-coated steel anchoring plates fix it to the ground, and Pro-Tect testing rates it for winds of up to 100 mph. Three electrical outlets and three USB ports sit in the patented PowerPort. Parts are pre-cut, pre-drilled and pre-stained, and the BILT app walks through the sequence.

This matters because the excerpt ships as the meta and OG description.

excerpt: A cedar gazebo under a sloped galvanized steel roof, Pro-Tect rated for 8,700 pounds of roof load and 100 mph winds, with a PowerPort for lighting and music.
description:
The Arcadia's roof is sloped galvanized steel, pitched so rain and meltwater run off instead of pooling on top, and finished to resist corrosion. Underneath it the frame is cedar, a wood naturally resistant to rot and decay, and the pieces arrive pre-stained.
Pro-Tect testing rates the structure for a roof load of up to 8,700 pounds and wind speeds up to 100 mph. A PowerPort supplies three electrical outlets plus USB ports for charging, lighting and music. Every board is pre-cut and pre-drilled before it ships, so the build is an assembly job rather than a woodworking one.

excerpt: A cedar gazebo with black steel accents beneath a 29-gauge galvanized steel peak roof, rated for 9,000 pounds of roof weight and winds of up to 100 mph.

A peak roof gives the Norwood its shape, and the roofing itself is 29-gauge galvanized steel, which resists dents and is protected against corrosion. Black steel accents pick out the lines of the frame, built from 100 percent cedar and naturally durable.
Pro-Tect testing rates the structure to hold up to 9,000 pounds of roof weight and to stand in wind speeds up to 100 mph. Under the peak there is shade through summer and cover when the weather turns. A PowerPort supplies three electrical outlets and three USB ports for lighting, music or charging. The kit is ready to assemble, with pre-cut, pre-drilled and pre-stained components and step-by-step guidance in the BILT app.

excerpt: A 16x12 cedar gazebo rated for 10,600 pounds of roof weight, roofed in 29-gauge galvanized steel and trimmed with black steel accents on the frame.

Roof weight is the number that stands out here. Pro-Tect testing rates the 16x12 Norwood to 10,600 pounds, along with wind speeds up to 100 mph. The roofing is 29-gauge galvanized steel, resistant to dents and protected against corrosion, and it rises to a peak that sheds weather and throws a good amount of shade.

excerpt: A cedar peak-roof gazebo whose PowerPort runs two USB-C ports and a USB-A alongside three outlets, rated for 9,000 pounds of roof weight and 100 mph winds.

The PowerPort on this gazebo runs three electrical outlets plus two USB-C ports and one USB-A, which covers most of what gets charged outdoors without an adapter hanging off a post.
Structurally it is 100 percent cedar, naturally durable, under a 29-gauge galvanized steel roof that resists dents and is protected from corrosion. Black steel accents trim the frame, and the peak shape gives shade in summer and cover when the weather turns. Pro-Tect testing rates it to 9,000 pounds of roof weight and wind speeds up to 100 mph. Components ship pre-cut, pre-drilled and pre-stained, and the BILT app runs through assembly step by step.

excerpt: Twelve feet of powder-coated galvanized steel, this Emory outdoor kitchen island carries a built-in griddle, a pizza oven, counter space and storage.
description:
This twelve-foot Emory island carries a built-in griddle and a built-in pizza oven, with spacious counter space and generous storage. The flat top handles everything a grill grate cannot, and the oven covers pizza and anything else that wants serious heat.
Range constructs the island from fully powder-coated galvanized steel and engineers it to live outdoors through extreme weather year-round. Every component is tested for real-world durability, from the appliances to the hinges, and the cabinetry runs on soft-close hardware.
The island comes ready to use, which skips both the modular piecing and the drawn-out custom build.

The opening now just says the island carries a built-in griddle and a built-in pizza oven with counter space and storage, asserting no positions. excerpt: A nine-foot outdoor kitchen island in powder-coated galvanized steel, this Emory is built around a single griddle, with counter space and storage too.

A single built-in griddle sits in this nine-foot Emory island, with counter space for prep and serving and storage in the cabinetry below. The flat top handles the food that would otherwise fall through grill grates.
Range builds the island from fully powder-coated galvanized steel and engineers it for extreme weather year-round, testing the structure, appliance and hardware rather than assuming they will hold up. Doors and drawers use soft-close hardware.
It arrives as a finished island rather than a set of modules to piece together, so there is no custom build to plan or wait on.

excerpt: The nine-foot Emory island keeps to one built-in grill, set in a fully powder-coated galvanized steel body engineered for year-round outdoor weather.

One built-in grill, nine feet of galvanized steel island, and a spacious countertop. It suits people who grill and would rather have the counter room than a second appliance.
The steel is fully powder-coated and engineered to stay outside in extreme weather all year. Range tests each component for real-world durability, down to the hinges, and the storage cabinetry uses soft-close hardware.

excerpt: The white Caraway Cottage from Backyard Discovery is a cedar playhouse for indoors or out, with a play kitchen, half door, flower box and chalkboard.
description:
Crisp white over cedar gives this Backyard Discovery playhouse its farmhouse character. The Caraway Cottage can be set up indoors or outside, and a working half door opens into it. Wide windows keep the interior bright and make it easy to check on play from a distance.
Inside is a fully equipped play kitchen for pretend cooking. Outside, a flower box sits below a window and a mailbox waits for make-believe letters, while a chalkboard adds a spot for drawing between games. The structure is cedar, which handles outdoor conditions and gives the white finish a solid base.

'its working half door lets kids swing the top open and lean out or shut themselves in' is now 'a working half door opens into it' — matching both the source ('a working half door') and how the sibling light-brown listing handles the same feature. excerpt: Maintenance-free steel Atlas playset with a twisting tube slide and a wave slide off one clubhouse deck, plus a rock wall and two belt swings.

The frame underneath is galvanized square-tube steel, powder coated, with wood-toned composite panels that never need staining or sealing and will not splinter, and the mower can run right up to it. The raised clubhouse has a peaked roof, and inside are a chalkboard, a steering wheel, and a telescope. Kids climb by the flat-step ladder with handrails or take the rock wall for something harder. A shaded play space under the deck holds a toy grill and play food, and the beam carries two belt swings and a metal trapeze. Backyard Discovery ships it ready to assemble with 3D instructions in the BILT app and covers every part for 5 years.

excerpt: Heavy-duty galvanized steel A-frame swing set with two coated-chain belt swings, a metal trapeze, molded feet with ground anchors, and a 5-year warranty.

The angled A-frame is what gives it stability, and the heavy-duty hardware is sized to match. Two belt swings hang on coated chains that stay comfortable to grip, with a metal trapeze bar beside them for hanging and flipping. The swing zone is extra large, leaving room for more than one child to swing at the same time without crowding. Molded feet and the included ground anchors hold the frame down as a freestanding structure. Pieces come pre-fabricated, pre-drilled, and powder coated for assembly, and the set carries a 5-year warranty. Galvanized steel also means weather does little to it and upkeep stays minimal.

I cut the height anyway because the complaint I was given named it and removing a detail cannot make the copy false — but it can be restored if that was a paraphrasing slip. 'Freestanding' is kept because this product's source highlight states 'Freestanding Setup'.

excerpt: Argentine-style open-fire grill for wood or charcoal, with height-adjustable steel grates, a 360-degree asado clamp, and a 12-gauge steel body.

The heavy-duty steel grates adjust to several heights, so you can drop them near the coals to sear or raise them away for slow cooking. A stainless-steel clamp locks into seven positions and rotates a full 360 degrees, and S-hooks let you hang sausages or ribs above the fire when the grates are full. Refractory fire bricks and ceramic fire blanket insulation hold heat in the chamber, while the brasero firebox infuses the food with the rich, smoky flavor that defines Argentine grilling. The body is 12-gauge powder-coated steel with an acacia wood side table and handles, and a lower rack stores firewood and supplies. A coal shovel is included. The grill ships ready to assemble, with each step guided in the interactive BILT app.

excerpt: Lodge gazebo in a 14x12 footprint, built from oversized cedar timber under a powder-coated galvanized steel roof engineered for demanding climates.

Oversized cedar timber carries the whole structure here, and at a 14x12 footprint the posts and beams are heavy enough that the gazebo reads as part of the yard rather than something set down on it. Steel gables and detailing balance that natural warmth with architectural precision.
The roof is galvanized steel with a powder-coated finish, engineered for demanding climates and performing reliably through high winds, heavy snow and year-round exposure. Every detail is intended to make the structure feel integral to the space rather than added to it.

excerpt: 16x14 Lodge gazebo with a powder-coated galvanized steel roof engineered for high winds and heavy snow, carried on oversized cedar posts and beams.

excerpt: The 19x14 Lodge gazebo carries oversized cedar posts and beams under a powder-coated galvanized steel roof engineered for demanding climates.

At 19x14 this Lodge gazebo runs long in one direction, and the extra span is where the weight of the oversized cedar timber shows. Substantial posts and beams give the structure a grounded presence and a sense of permanence.
Galvanized steel forms the roof, finished in powder coat, and it is engineered for demanding climates that bring high winds, heavy snow and year-round exposure. Steel gables and detailing carry across the longer elevation, balancing that natural warmth with architectural precision.

excerpt: An 8-foot by 6-foot privacy screen in cedar and aluminum that blocks sightlines on a deck, balcony or garden path while still letting a breeze through.
description:
